rationale:
Partly accepted the round-1 critique. Evidence is still only the contract, since no race telemetry exists yet, so every expected result below is a hypothesis to test, not an observed outcome.

Changed:
1) Speed. Accepted that base_speed 1.6 leaves no margin for a 3.0 s finish on a 4 to 5 m course, which needs an average of about 1.5 m/s with wheel lag and slip. Raised base_speed to 1.9 (base_pwm about 3886, 95 percent). It stays below the 2.0 ceiling, which is where extra speed stops having effect, and it leaves some headroom for bends.
2) Steering gain. Accepted the correction that the signal is a weighted average in weight units, not metres. A 12 mm offset gives a signal near 0.75, so kp 3 already gives a turn near 2.25 (about 790 PWM counts). I lowered kp to 2.5 to reduce overshoot at the higher speed. Turn near 1.9 for the same offset, still a firm correction.
3) Derivative. Accepted that kd 0.3 is dominated by sensor-edge jumps (about 30 turn units per edge). Reduced kd to 0.03, which keeps a small damping action without a large kick on each edge.
4) Integral. Accepted that ki 0 leaves a steady drift from the fixed motor mismatch. Set ki to 0.1. Its maximum contribution is capped at about 0.2 turn units because the integral is limited to plus or minus 2, so it removes bias without windup.
5) Sensor lead. Moved the sensor row from y 0.04 to y 0.06 to give about 37 ms of lead at 1.9 m/s, which matters more at higher speed.

Kept: five sensors at 16 mm spacing with x from -0.032 to +0.032 and size 0.012, so the 25 mm tape is always covered. Weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2) keep the sign convention. line_loss last_direction is kept, because the tape is always on one side after a bend. The body and mass are kept as mid-range values. The critique showed body_width has no useful effect on the off-track limit at these values, so I did not change it.

Not accepted: I did not move to a much higher speed or remove kd completely, because the critique gave no evidence that either is required. The racing data will show whether 1.9 is too fast.

Expected result (hypothesis): completion on the development tracks with average speed of about 1.5 to 1.7 m/s, rms_error under about 0.03 m, and no more than a few line-loss events. The main test is whether the higher speed causes oscillation or off-track runs on the S-bend and slalom. If steering_oscillation or max_error is high, the next step is to lower base_speed first, then kp.
